mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 4.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity cash flows and producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.2 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.01 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous 3-month increases in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.1% indicate robust economic expansion, driving corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and INDPRO both rise > 0.1% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 50% of instances when HOUST and INDPRO both rise > 0.1% in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.5%) combined with elevated interest rates (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) triggers aggressive monetary tightening, suppressing risk appetite and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and high rate regime
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.5% and FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or Rank IC < 0.01 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) above 0.5% reflects strong economic activity, supporting corporate profits and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 40% of instances when GDPC1 increases > 0.5% quarterly, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 100.0 signals manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate revenue expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 50% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0, or Rank IC < 0.01 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Tight labor markets (UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly) fuel consumer spending, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days despite inflationary pressures.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 50% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent 3-month increases in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) above 0.1% indicate robust consumer demand, driving economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both rise > 0.1% in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in > 50% of instances when RSAFS and HOUST both rise > 0.1% in 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year windows.
